results.controlIntent: Employ [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals multiple failures against CM-3(1) sub-controls:

**Sub-control (d) — Prohibit changes until designated approvals are received [FAILED]:**
The most critical finding is the `UpdateEndpoint` event (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z, event ID `3f5af7ae`) deploying config `churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`. The model registry (`5392106c`) contains only one entry (v1, approved 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z) with no corresponding approval record for this hotfix change. This means a production change was executed without a prior registry approval — a direct violation of the gate-keeping requirement.

**Sub-controls (a), (b), (c), (f) — Documentation, notification, highlighting, and completion notification [INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE / NOT DEMONSTRATED]:**
No evidence was retrieved showing: (a) automated documentation of proposed changes; (b) automated notification to approval authorities; (c) automated highlighting of changes pending approval beyond a defined time period; or (f) automated notification to personnel upon completion of approved changes. The CloudTrail events show raw API calls by an IAM user (`data-scientist-jdoe`) with no evidence of an automated change-management workflow orchestrating these steps.

**Initial deployment (CreateEndpoint, 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z):** The endpoint was created ~2 hours *after* the registry approval timestamp (09:00Z), so temporal ordering for the initial deployment is consistent with an approval-before-deploy sequence. However, this alone does not demonstrate that an automated mechanism enforced the gate — it could have been a manual coincidence.

**Overall:** The unapproved hotfix deployment is a clear, documented violation. The absence of any evidence of automated change-control mechanisms (notification, gating, documentation workflows) means the control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated mechanism enforcing approval gating (e.g., EventBridge rule, Lambda gate, or CI/CD pipeline policy) before endpoint changes are permitted
No evidence of automated notification to approval authorities when changes are proposed (sub-control b)
No evidence of automated alerting for changes pending approval beyond a defined time window (sub-control c)
No evidence of automated completion notifications to designated personnel (sub-control f)
No registry entry or approval record for the 2026-03-15 hotfix deployment — human attestation needed to determine whether an out-of-band approval process exists
Only one model package version in the registry; it is unclear whether the hotfix config was intentionally excluded or whether the registry is not being used as the system of record for all changes
